key_insight: This paper asks whether AI agents can reliably carry out quantum engineering tasks, not just suggest ideas. The core insight is that autonomy in quantum labs must be evaluated by verification, because success depends on both planning and trustworthy execution in a highly complex physical setting.
problem_solved: It addresses the growing burden of manually characterizing, operating, and coordinating quantum experiments as platforms scale up. The paper tackles the question of how to assess whether scientific AI agents can actually perform these tasks reliably in quantum engineering workflows.
method: Defines a verification-focused perspective for autonomous quantum engineering instead of only measuring task completion.
Evaluates AI agents across the stages of planning experiments, operating instruments, and analyzing observations.
Uses quantum engineering as a realistic testbed to probe reliability, coordination, and practical autonomy.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights that benchmark design must include reliability and verification, especially in safety- or precision-critical domains. It also shows how agentic systems may need stronger evaluation standards before they can be trusted in real scientific workflows.

paper_title: Evaluating Verified Autonomy in Quantum Engineering
paper_authors: Naixu Guo, Changhao Li, Siyu Cheng, Qicheng Tang, Binzhao Luo
